results.title: DigitalOcean pricing: bundled plans vs v5 hourly | ToolBistro
highlights:
Published 2026-11-04 · Researched and price-checked on official sources

DigitalOcean pricing starts at $4/mo for a 512 MiB Droplet and $6/mo for 1 GiB, both capped at 672 billable hours per month. The newer v5 configurations bill per resource with no cap, so 1 vCPU and 1 GiB runs about $17 over a 730-hour month. All rates below were verified on 4 November 2026.

...

## DigitalOcean GPU Droplet pricing

GPU Droplets are a different catalog, and the per-hour rates are quoted per GPU rather than per machine. On-demand prices listed in the docs on 4 November 2026:

- NVIDIA RTX 4000: $0.76/hr. L40s and RTX 6000: $1.57/hr.
- AMD MI300X: $2.59/hr. AMD MI325X: $3.80/hr.
- NVIDIA H100: $4.41/hr. H200: $4.47/hr.
- 8x variants scale up, for example 8x H200 at $35.76/hr.

DigitalOcean also advertises GPU Droplets from $1.91 per GPU hour on a multi-month contractual commitment, which is worth pricing against the on-demand rate if you are running inference continuously rather than in bursts. Spot GPU Droplets sit in public preview at rates that change daily and are always at or below on-demand: an air-cooled B300 lists at $6.17/hr and an MI355X at $4.50/hr. DigitalOcean can reclaim a spot instance with two hours' notice.

The billing rule is the same as CPU: per second with a 60-second minimum, and a powered-off GPU Droplet keeps billing until destroyed. Newer accounts may also see a mid-cycle charge when a GPU Droplet is created, which the docs describe as an anti-abuse measure that does not change the total.

results.title: GPU cloud cost comparison: H100, H200, L40S per hour
results.author: Cloud Provider Benchmarks Research
highlights:
Published: 6 November 2026 Updated: 6 November 2026 Türkçe oku 

Direct answer

Among the published USD list prices at the access date, the L40S is the lowest-cost GPU per hour and the H200 the highest. Per TB/s of memory bandwidth, however, the published H100 and H200 prices are lower than the L40S. Compare across currencies only after applying current exchange rates and tax treatment.

## Executive summary 

This analysis lists the published on-demand list prices per GPU-hour for H100, H200 and L40S at the tracked providers, each with its source and access date, and normalises them per GB of GPU memory and per TB/s of memory bandwidth. Prices stay in each provider's own currency and billing basis. Several providers offer a GPU without publishing an hourly price; they appear as available but unpriced.

## Key findings

1. 01 Prices are published in different currencies (USD and TRY), so no cross-provider ranking is computed on this page.
2. 02 Billing granularity differs: per second with a minimum charge, per minute, or hourly. Short jobs can cost more than the hourly price implies on coarse billing.
3. 03 Some GPUs are offered without public prices (for example PortvMind H200/L40S and several hyperscaler configurations); they are marked as unpriced rather than estimated.
4. 04 Per-GPU-hour list prices exclude storage, data transfer and host resources that some providers bundle and others bill separately.

## Published prices

Every row below comes from the provider’s own pricing page, with the access date linked to the source. The basis column explains what the price covers.

## Why there is no single ranking

- Currency. PortvMind lists prices in Turkish lira excluding tax; the other providers list in US dollars. Converting at a fixed rate would make the page wrong within weeks.
- Configuration. Some providers sell one GPU per instance; others price an 8-GPU node and the per-GPU figure assumes the full node.
- Billing granularity. DigitalOcean bills per second with a 60-second minimum, PortvMind bills per minute, and Vultr bills hourly. Hetzner bills per started hour with a monthly cap but does not offer these GPU models.
- Bundled resources. vCPU, host RAM and local NVMe are included at some providers and priced separately at others.

## How the bill works

- By the second: billing starts when you create the Droplet and stops when you destroy it, with 60 seconds at least.
- Powered off is still billed: the GPU stays reserved for you, so switching the Droplet off does not stop the charge.
- No monthly ceiling: the 672-hour monthly cap of DigitalOcean's ordinary Droplets does not apply to GPU Droplets.
- Spot machines: in public preview, at a daily price never above on-demand. DigitalOcean gives at least 2 hours' notice before it takes one back.
- Data transfer: incoming traffic and traffic inside your private network are free. Outgoing traffic above your team's pooled allowance is billed by the gigabyte.

New accounts may be charged partway through the month when they create GPU Droplets. DigitalOcean says the total does not change.

results.title: GPU Cloud Prices October 2026: H100, A100, L40S Across 16 Providers
results.author: Bo Shen
highlights:
We collected on-demand GPU list prices from 16 cloud providers three times a day from October 7 to 19, 2026. List prices barely moved: 14 of 407 tracked offers changed. The spread between providers is the real ... And 13 of 22 H100 listings didn't say whether the card is SXM, PCIe or NVL, a difference worth 2.25× in served tokens in our tests.

...
